notes: Archive only (R-128's stage-B cells, five lineages x 24 shared manifests, 3,072 cases each); no episode, no model call; definitions committed (867bf43) before the audit ran. Among reconstructed-triggered cases still in play 30 steps after support ends (863-995 per lineage), the rolling-step fraction rises by 0.166 / 0.321 / 0.186 / 0.092 / 0.313 across the end of support in lineages 0-4. Lineage 2's change minus the mean of the other four is -0.037, 95% interval [-0.064, -0.011] (manifest-clustered [-0.057, -0.014]): the upper bound is far below +0.10, so the hypothesis is REFUTED; lineage 2 shows, if anything, slightly less release-associated improvement. The premise was also off at this stage: all five stage-B modules have long ramp-outs (22-42 steps) and stroke multipliers near 1 (1.01-1.23), so lineage 2 (42.4, 1.02) is not distinctive after 12 updates; its long ramp-out only stands out at the later stages. Triggers are reconstructed, one lineage is one lineage, and the comparison is an association around the end of support.
